title: Baked Chicken Breast Loaf Pan Bake
description: Spiced, yogurt-marinated chicken packed into a loaf pan and baked so it steams in its own juices — comes out sliceable and moist. Great over rice or in pita for easy meals throughout the week.
ingredients: 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (up to 1/2 tsp for more heat)
1/2 large lemon, juiced (about 1.5 tbsp lemon juice)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Trim any excess fat from 2.5 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast and cut into large chunks or strips. Place in a large bowl.

Drizzle the chicken with 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, then season with salt and black pepper to taste, 1.5 tbsp garlic powder, 1.5 tbsp sweet paprika, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, 1 tbsp dried oregano, 1 tbsp Aleppo pepper, 1/2 tsp ground cumin, and 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon.
Add 2 tbsp plain Greek yogurt, 1.5 tbsp tomato paste, and the juice of 1/2 large lemon (about 1.5 tbsp lemon juice). Mix everything together well until the chicken is fully coated.
Thinly slice 1/2 large yellow onion and mix it in with the chicken. Cover and marinate in the fridge for 2-3 hours, or overnight for best flavor. If short on time, you can cook it right away.
Preheat oven to 425°F. Let the marinated chicken come to room temperature while you pack it tightly into a loaf pan (approx. 8.5 x 4.5 x 2.5 inches).
Bake for 35-40 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 160°F. Because breast is leaner than thigh, check a few minutes early to avoid overcooking.
Remove from the oven and let the pan rest, tented loosely with foil, for 5 minutes — the internal temperature will climb to a safe 165°F as it rests.
Tilt the pan over a glass container to pour off the excess juices; spoon these back over the chicken before serving, or save as a soup base.
Flip the loaf pan out onto a cutting board, slice the chicken into strips, and serve over rice, in pita, or alongside roasted vegetables.
notes: Protein-per-100-calorie ratio is ~16.2g, right at the high-protein benchmark. Fat comes in very low (7g/serving) since breast replaces thigh, leaving plenty of room in a daily fat budget. Packing the chicken tightly into the loaf pan is what keeps lean breast from drying out — it essentially steams in its own marinade juices. If the chicken pieces are very thick, an instant-read thermometer is the safest way to judge doneness rather than relying on time alone.
